title: The Fixed Point Reached by Repeatedly Taking Cosines
originalTopic: Fixed-point iteration and convergence to the Dottie number
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Starting with x_0 = 1 and repeatedly pressing the cosine key (radians), the display settles to a single number. Explain why the iteration x_{n+1} = cos(x_n) converges, identify the equation its limit satisfies, and give the limiting value.
finalAnswer: x \approx 0.739085 \quad (\text{the unique solution of } x = \cos x)

steps.title: Run the iteration and watch it settle
steps.explanation: Successive values oscillate with shrinking amplitude and by the tenth iterate already agree with 0.739 to several decimals.
steps.why: Numerical iteration is often the only way to see a fixed point, since x = cos x has no closed-form algebraic solution.

steps.title: Show the fixed point is unique
steps.mathExpression: g(x) = \cos x - x, \qquad g'(x) = -\sin x - 1 \le 0, \quad g' < 0 \ \text{except at isolated points}
steps.explanation: The function g is strictly decreasing, and since g(0) = 1 > 0 while g(1) = cos(1) - 1 approx -0.4597 < 0, it crosses zero exactly once.
steps.why: Monotonicity plus a sign change proves the calculator is converging to the one and only solution, not to one of several.

steps.title: Explain convergence with the slope at the fixed point
steps.explanation: Near the limit the error is multiplied by about 0.67 each step, so the iteration is a contraction and the errors decay geometrically.
steps.why: A fixed-point iteration converges precisely when the absolute derivative of the iterating function is less than 1 at the fixed point.

steps.title: Read the answer graphically
steps.explanation: Plotting both curves on [-1, 2] by [-1, 2] shows a single crossing at x approximately 0.739085, and the staircase of iterates drawn between the curves spirals into that point.
steps.why: The cobweb picture connects the calculator's numeric behavior to the geometric meaning of a fixed point as an intersection with y = x.
